subject: Music Production
title: Bridgeport Music v. Dimension Films
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Bridgeport Music v. Dimension Films.

hook.text: NWA sampled a two-second guitar riff from Funkadelic, and the case reached a federal appeals court.

buildup.text: The court had to decide if sampling even a tiny fragment required permission from the original owner.

discovery.text: The ruling declared 'Get a license or do not sample,' making even tiny snippets legally risky.

twist.text: This strict ruling pushed many producers to recreate sounds instead of sampling them directly.

climax.text: The case created the strictest sampling law standard in the world and changed production practices.

punchline.text: Two seconds of guitar rewrote sampling law forever.

quiz.question: What did the Bridgeport ruling famously state?
options: Get a license or do not sample
